newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says won't hurry large bank privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says won't hurry large bank privatisation.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Wednesday that there was no reason to hurry the privatisation of the country's four largest banks.
"(The privatisation of banks) does not have any exceptional level of urgency," Klaus told a news conference after a cabinet meeting.

He added that he did not "see a reason to hurry" and that the cabinet would wait until the central bank submitted a complete plan to the cabinet for the privatisation of the remaining state shares in the large banks.
"It is irrelevant if it is two or three weeks later or two or three weeks sooner," Klaus said.
The central bank and the finance ministry have both called for the rapid privatisation of the state's roughly one-third stake in Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. to a strategic foreign partner.
Japan-based investment bank Nomura and Dutch ING Bank NV are both said to have a strong interest in the IPB stake.
The Czech National Bank, the central bank, also has called for the merger of the largest savings bank Ceska Sporitelna a.s., with the foreign trade bank Ceskovslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s..
That plan calls for privatising the new combined megabank, which would be the largest institution in post-Communist Europe, several years after the merger is completed.
The central bank has said it would prefer to take a slower approach to the privatisation of Komercni Banka a.s. which it says does not require a strategic partner.
The state, through the National Property Fund, owns a roughly 49 percent stake in Komercni Banka.
